rows.label: Families receiving relief item distributions, 2025
rows.explainer: Families who got MSF's relief items (shelter material, blankets, mats, jerrycans, cooking sets, hygiene kits, mosquito nets) in 2025, MSF's count. Read by MSF's medical model (which subtracts the relief work) and its relief model, so the two always split the spending in full.

rows.label: Cost of a family's relief-item distribution, items and delivery (euros)
rows.explainer: MSF doesn't split its spending by activity or publish kit prices, so the relief distributions' cost is the families reached times a cost per family, our judgment: 45 euros. The public anchor is UK for UNHCR's family emergency survival kit (three blankets, three mats, two jerrycans, a kitchen set, two mosquito nets, two plastic sheets and a solar lamp) at £65, about 76 euros (https://shop.unrefugees.org.uk/products/emergency-survival-kit), a donor gift price for a full kit; MSF's average is lower because many of its distributions are hygiene or water kits only and it buys in bulk through MSF Supply, though transport and staff in insecure areas add to it. Low end a hygiene kit only; high end the full UNHCR kit with delivery. About 1.5% of programme spending at the best guess. Read by MSF's medical model (which subtracts the relief work) and its relief model, so the two always split the spending in full.

rows.label: Equipment and services sold to other organisations, 2025 (euros)

source.title: MSF International Financial Report 2025 (combined, audited, year to 31 December 2025)
source.quote: Equipment and services sold to other organisations by MSF Supply and MSF Logistique 11,764

rows.explainer: Supplies and services MSF Supply and MSF Logistique sell to other organisations; the buyers pay for them. Read by all three MSF models: their overhead ratio leaves the goods sold out (the buyers pay for them and their overhead), and the medical model counts only MSF's net cost of them.
